about.title: San Ramon Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A fall rarely feels like a legal matter in the moment. You are on the ground in a grocery aisle off Bollinger Canyon Road, or on a slick stairwell at an office building near Crow Canyon Road, and your first reaction is embarrassment, then pain. Only later does the real question surface: who was responsible for that hazard? Under California premises liability law, a property owner or manager can be held accountable when they knew, or reasonably should have known, about a hazardous condition and failed to fix it or warn people. That "notice" element is where San Ramon claims are usually won or lost, and it depends on evidence that disappears fast: surveillance footage, incident reports, cleaning logs, witness names. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect people injured in Contra Costa County with an independent personal injury attorney who takes premises cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. The general two-year filing window shrinks when a public entity owns the property, which is one more reason to reach out sooner rather than later.

whyChoose.title: Why San Ramon Fall Victims Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Notice Is the Whole Case
items.desc: California requires proof that the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. The attorneys in our network know how to pursue maintenance records, inspection schedules, and prior complaints that show what the property manager was aware of.

items.title: Video Does Not Wait
items.desc: Many San Ramon retail centers and office parks overwrite surveillance footage within days. An attorney can send a preservation demand quickly so the recording of your fall, and the minutes before it, is not lost.

items.title: Deadlines Are Shorter Than People Think
items.desc: You generally have two years to file, but a fall on city, county, or other public property triggers a much shorter claim process. Comparative fault rules also mean the other side will look for ways to shift blame onto you, so early guidance helps.

items.question: I slipped in a shopping center parking lot along San Ramon Valley Boulevard. Who is actually liable?
items.answer: It depends on who controls that part of the property. The center owner, a property management company, an individual tenant, or a maintenance contractor could each carry responsibility for the spot where you fell. An attorney can review lease terms and maintenance agreements to identify the right party, then determine whether they had notice of the hazard.

items.question: The store says I was not watching where I was going. Does that end my claim?
items.answer: No. California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you are found partly at fault, you can still recover damages reduced by your percentage of responsibility. The owner's argument does not erase their own duty to address a hazard they knew or should have known about. What matters is the evidence, not the store's initial position.

items.question: What should I do in the first few days after a fall in San Ramon?
items.answer: Get medical care first, even if the pain seems manageable, since hip and back injuries often worsen over time. Photograph the hazard and the surrounding area if you can, ask for a written incident report, and note the names of anyone who saw it happen. Then reach out to an attorney promptly so a request to preserve surveillance video goes out before the footage is recorded over.
